svg.title: Second day after hip surgery. A 72-year-old man is sitting up, restless, and says he cannot get a deep breath. Respirations 28 and shallow, oxygen saturation 86 percent on room air, heart rate 108, blood pressure 138/84, temperature 37.2 degrees C. Crackles at both bases. Incision pain 3 of 10. He refuses the incentive spirometer.
svg.desc: An oxygen saturation of 86 percent is hypoxemia; StatPearls gives 95 to 100 percent as the normal adult range and calls anything under 90 percent hypoxemia. Sitting him upright and giving prescribed oxygen fix the gas exchange problem, and saturation plus work of breathing tell you whether it worked. Anxiety is the tempting condition because he is restless, but restlessness is an early sign of low oxygen rather than proof of panic. Breathing into a paper bag would lower his oxygen further.
